sources.notes: Source: Poddar et al., Cureus 18(3):e104772 (2026), KIMS Bhubaneswar, Odisha; retrospective sterile-body-fluid antibiogram, Jan 2021-Dec 2022. 2307 samples, 291 isolates (12.6% positive); GPC 54%, S. aureus most common (92/291), MRSA 48.9%; K. pneumoniae top GNB (40), E. coli (27), Acinetobacter (24), Pseudomonas (19). All susceptibility data are presented ONLY as unlabeled bar charts (Fig 1 = Gram-positive: S. aureus, CONS, Enterococcus; Fig 2 = Gram-negative: K. pneumoniae, E. coli, Pseudomonas spp., Acinetobacter spp.) plus narrative sentences. There are NO numeric susceptibility tables. Method: rendered figure pages with PyMuPDF at 6x, calibrated the y-axis from detected tick-label centers (Fig 2: 0%=y1383, 100%=y368; Fig 1 baseline y1504), then extracted each bar's top and mid-bar color programmatically. Color->drug map validated by matching extracted values to the paper's own text (Acinetobacter imipenem 41.9 vs 'imipenem 41%', gentamicin 41.5 vs 'aminoglycosides 41%', cotrimoxazole 36.8 vs '37.5%', ciprofloxacin 36.8 vs '38%'; E. coli ciprofloxacin 10.8 vs 'ciprofloxacin resistance high 90%'; Pseudomonas ceftazidime 20.9 vs '21%', ciprofloxacin 9.9 vs '10-11%'). Values are %
issues: Staph aureus text-derived cells (linezolid 95.65, dapto 95, TGC 92, VA/TEI 90.21): the paper states these for 'Staphylococcus spp.' collectively (Fig 1 has separate S. aureus and CoNS bar groups). Assigning them specifically to S. aureus is a reasonable but not certain mapping; the 95.65% 'highest' value could belong to either Staph group.

Pseudomonas amikacin s=20.9 is read as LOWER than meropenem/cefepime (25.9), but the text explicitly says Pseudomonas showed 'highest sensitivity to amikacin, followed by carbapenems' — i.e., amikacin should exceed the carbapenems. Bar-read ordering is inconsistent with the text; value is approximate so not force-corrected, but flag for review.

Klebsiella ampicillin s=41.9 (bar read) is clinically implausible since K. pneumoniae is intrinsically ampicillin-resistant (expected ~0%); cannot confirm from the rendered bar chart. Possible misread of the AMP bar.
Oxacillin s=51.1 is a valid 100-R conversion from MRSA 48.9% (45/92); direction correct.

All remaining Gram-negative per-drug numbers are pixel reads off Figure 2 bar chart and cannot be independently confirmed to the stated decimal precision; they are appropriately flagged approx and are broadly consistent with the text ranges (amikacin 41-63%, carbapenems 40-60%, E. coli cipro ~10%).

Source reports susceptibility ONLY as qualitative bands: highly sensitive >=80%, moderately sensitive 60-80%, poorly sensitive <60% (Table 3, page 4). No S/I/R counts, no exact per-drug percentages EXCEPT Tobramycin vs Acinetobacter = 96% (only exact figure printed). For 60-80% bands I stored midpoint s=70 with approx:true; for <60% bands I left s=null and used qualitative q (no lower bound given, so a number would be a guess); for the single 'carbapenems strong 80%' Pseudomonas statement I stored s=80 approx. 'Carbapenems' is a class - only meropenem was tested (methods: 'Meropenem and minocycline used as reserved drugs'), so mapped to meropenem with note. 'Cephalosporins (1st-3rd gen)' is a class - recorded as ceftazidime + ceftriaxone (the named first-line cephalosporins) with note. Cefoperazone-sulbactam and ceftazidime-avibactam kept as printed combo tokens (not plain cefoperazone/ceftazidime). n values are Table-2 TOTAL ICU isolate counts per genus (E.coli 244, Klebsiella 277, Pseudomonas 148, Acinetobacter 93, Proteus 13); T
issues: This is a banded/qualitative antibiogram, not numeric. Table 3 gives ranges (>=80% highly, 60-80% moderately, <60% poorly). The extraction represents the 60-80% band as s=70 (midpoint) and flags approx=true; the 80% cell (Pseudomonas carbapenems) as s=80; and <60% cells as s=null. This is a defensible modeling choice but no exact percentages exist in the source except Tobramycin/Acinetobacter (96%

SOURCE INTERNAL CONFLICT (E. coli, cefoperazone-sulbactam): Table 3 lists cefoperazone-sulbactam under E. coli's <60% (poorly sensitive) column, but the page-3 narrative states 'cefoperazone-sulbactam, other reserved agents such as carbapenems and minocycline exhibited moderate sensitivity (60-80%)' for E. coli. The extraction followed Table 3 (s=null, <60%), which is the correct primary tabular s

SOURCE INTERNAL CONFLICT (Klebsiella, nitrofurantoin): Table 3 lists Nitrofurantoin as the effective urinary drug for Klebsiella, but page-3 narrative says 'nitrofurantoin showed low sensitivity.' Extraction followed Table 3 (effective) and explicitly documents the conflict. Acceptable.

SOURCE INTERNAL CONFLICT (Pseudomonas & Acinetobacter urinary agents): Table 3 lists Nitrofurantoin+Norfloxacin as effective urinary drugs for both Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter, and page-4 narrative agrees ('effective against Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter'), yet page-3 narrative says these agents 'showed inadequate sensitivity'/'demonstrated limited efficacy' for these organisms. Extraction omitt

MINOR over-specification: the paper names organisms only at genus level for the ICU cohort (Klebsiella, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Proteus). The extraction assigns species (K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa, A. baumannii, P. mirabilis). These are reasonable inferences (species named elsewhere in discussion) but are not stated for the antibiogram itself. No susceptibility impact.

All n values, band assignments, and drug mappings verified correct against Table 2 and Table 3. Meropenem <60% for Acinetobacter (explicit in Table 3 poorly-sensitive column), Tobramycin 96% for Acinetobacter, and Pseudomonas carbapenems 80% are all accurately captured. No hallucinated cells and no %R<->%S direction errors.

sources.notes: Source: Muthusamy R, Mahesh S, Travasso C. 'Antibiotic Profiling of E. coli Borne UTI Infection in Tertiary Healthcare Settings.' Cureus 16(3):e56632, 2024 (Saveetha Medical College, Chennai). Text extracted with PyMuPDF (6 pages, digital text, fully readable). Study: 80 urine samples from female patients (35-50 yr), 44 UTI-positive, 18 E. coli-positive. ONLY quantitative AST is Table 1 (page 3): zone-of-inhibition in mm for FOUR individual E. coli strains (1B2602, 1B2453, 1B2695, 1R578) with legend '* Sensitive, -- Resistant' (bare numbers without asterisk are ambiguous/not flagged sensitive). This is NOT a percentage-susceptible antibiogram: no %S or %R is printed for any drug across the 18 isolates, and per-drug denominators are only 1-4 strains with inconsistent/partial testing. I therefore did NOT compute or emit any numeric s values (would require fabricating a population statistic from n<=4). All s set null; q captures the printed per-strain qualitative verdict where clear. Methods section names only nitrofurantoin/cephalosporin/cephalexin discs (contradicting the wider drug list in Table 1) and states high resistance to these three, but gives no numeric value. sources.notes: Source: TARS-Net Telangana State AMR Surveillance Annual Report 2024 (nodal centre Osmania Medical College), 13 sentinel sites, 10 districts, 16,274 isolates (15,674 unique-patient after dedup), Jan 1–Dec 31 2024. Tables report %RESISTANT (%R) per specimen column; ALL s-values here were converted s=100−R (from_R:true). Guidelines: CLSI. Specimen scope for each organism entry is the table's per-specimen N (BLOOD or URINE). I extracted blood (sterile-site benchmark) for all six core organisms, plus urine for E. coli, Klebsiella and Enterococcus (UTI-relevant). Tables 6–11 = S.aureus/Enterococcus/E.coli/Klebsiella/Pseudomonas/Acinetobacter. Report labels genus-level "Klebsiella species", "Pseudomonas species", "Acinetobacter species", "Enterococcus species" (species not split) — mapped to K. pneumoniae / P. aeruginosa / A. baumannii as the dominant species and to generic "Enterococcus". MRSA context: cefoxitin %R (methicillin surrogate) = 53% in blood, 43% in pus, 100% in OSBF(n=4) for S. aureus; so MRSA ~53% among blood isolates. VRE: Enterococcus vancomycin %R = 3% blood, 0.26% urine, 2% pus. Linezolid 0%R across all specimens for both S.aureus and Enterococcus. Colistin 0%R (100%S)

sources.notes: Cureus 2026 (Mohod et al.), IGGMC Nagpur; study period May 2024–April 2025; 4603 culture-positive isolates. Tables 2-4 (pages 6-8) report % RESISTANT — all s values converted as s=100-R (from_R:true). IR=intrinsic resistance, NR=not recommended by CLSI, NT=not tested, MIC=only MIC recommended, U=tested only in urinary isolates — these cells omitted or marked. E. coli/K. pneumoniae from Table 2 (lactose-fermenting GNB); P. aeruginosa/Acinetobacter from Table 3 (non-lactose-fermenters) — 'Acinetobacter spp.' mapped to Acinetobacter baumannii per scope. S. aureus/Enterococcus faecalis/faecium from Table 4. Colistin 0%R = 100%S all GNB. MRSA = 48.72% (matches S. aureus cefoxitin 48%R → 52%S). VRE 0.77%. Salmonella Typhi (n=11) figures from narrative prose on page 7 (not tabulated): ampicillin 78%R, cefotaxime 49%R, azithromycin 64%R, levofloxacin 64%R, cotrimoxazole 46%R. Nitrofurantoin/Fosfomycin tested only in urinary isolates. penicillin and high-level-gentamicin (hlg) use non-list tokens.
